newsitem.title: USA: U.S. commission approves BG&E and PEPCO merger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. commission approves BG&E and PEPCO merger.

text.p: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and the Maryland Public Service Commission Wednesday both approved the merger of Baltimore Gas and Electric Co. and Potomac Electric Power Co.

While critics of the $2.9 billion merger had raised concern that the new company, Constellation Energy, would have too much control over local power markets, neither commission ordered the utilities to sell off any of their power plants.
The Maryland commission required, however, the two utilities to cut their rates by a total of $56 million and freeze the new rates for three years.
The state commission also ordered Constellation, which would be the 10th largest U.S. utility, to give customers half of any earnings it gained in excess of a 11.4 percent return on equity.
Baltimore Gas and Electric provided gas and power in Maryland, while Washington-based Potomac Electric provides power in the Washington and nearby areas of Maryland.

The conditions for sharing gains from the merger between customers and shareholders were more in line with demands by consumers, who battled the proposal, than with the utilities' offer, said Maryland People's Counsel Michael Travieso.

A spokeswoman for the two companies said they had no immediate opinion on the Maryland commission's order. "We need to analyse it ... to make sure the benefits of the merger will be fully realised," said spokeswoman Nancy Moses.
While saying that the union would not affect competition in the wholesale power market in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland power pool area, the FERC warned it could harm local consumers.
"We do see cause for concern at the retail level," FERC Chairwoman Elizabeth Moler said.
But the FERC deferred to Maryland and District of Columbia regulators to decide how to deal with Constellation's potential grip on the local market.

The Maryland commission said only that the "merger will allow the combined company to provide service more efficiently and effectively, and that the merger would produce financial savings that should be shared with ratepayers."
The District of Columbia has yet to rule on the merger, which the utilities aim to complete before July.
